cohort: The study included 43 pregnant women with uterine fibroids who underwent caesarean myomectomy with LSCS (case group) and 86 pregnant women with uterine fibroids who underwent LSCS alone (control group).
finding: Caesarean myomectomy was associated with a significantly higher incidence of hemorrhage, longer surgery duration, and longer hospital stay compared to LSCS alone.
mod_finding: Caesarean myomectomy, a specific mode of birth intervention, significantly increased hemorrhage and length of surgery and hospital stay compared to LSCS alone.
